swap_rate_curve.text:
`nelson_siegel_curve_fit` starts from yields you observe at various maturities and fits a smooth four-parameter curve (`beta0`, `beta1`, `beta2`, `tau`) to them, so it answers "what smooth curve describes these observed yields?" By contrast, `swap_rate_curve` starts from a curve of discount factors and works out the par swap rate for each tenor, so it answers "what fixed rate makes a swap worth zero, given these discount factors?"

The inputs differ accordingly. The fit takes `maturities` and `yields`, plus an optional starting guess `tau_init` for the decay. The swap function takes `discount_factors` and `maturities`, plus the fixed-leg payment `frequency`. One function summarizes market yields as a fitted shape, while the other converts an existing discount curve into swap rates.

explain.text: `nelson_siegel_curve_fit` fits a Nelson-Siegel yield curve to yields you observe at various maturities. You supply `maturities` (in years) and `yields` (as decimals), and optionally `tau_init`, an initial guess for the decay parameter. The curve is described by `beta0` (level), `beta1` (slope), `beta2` (curvature) and `tau` (decay). In this setup `beta0` is the asymptotic long rate, and `beta0 + beta1` is the instantaneous short rate. It's useful for smoothing a set of market yields into a compact curve.

when.text:
`nelson_siegel_curve_fit` (Nelson Siegel Curve Fit) fits a smooth four-parameter curve to yields you have observed, so it suits these situations:

- You have yields at a handful of maturities and want a smooth curve that summarises them, described by `beta0` (level), `beta1` (slope), `beta2` (curvature) and `tau` (decay).
- You want to read off the short end (`beta0 + beta1`) and the long-run level (`beta0`) of the curve in a compact form.
- You have observed `maturities` (in years, above zero) and matching `yields` as decimals, and are happy to start the decay search from `tau_init` or leave it at its default.
- You want to compare curve shapes over time using just a few parameters.

If you need a richer, six-parameter shape instead, `nelson_siegel_svensson_curve` fits the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson (six-parameter) curve.
